name: Latvia
tagline: Riga, one university at a time
summary: Latvia has no central application for international students: you apply to each institution on its own terms and its own calendar. The dates range widely — SSE Riga closes in early April with its own entrance test, Rīga Stradiņš closes Medicine for EU applicants on 1 July, and Turība takes autumn applications until 1 August.
whyConsider: Some English-taught options close after IB results, which is rare in Europe — Turība's autumn window runs to 1 August.
SSE Riga is a small, selective, test-based business school with results published in June.
watchOuts: Every institution sets its own deadline, test and fee. Rīga Stradiņš closes five days before IB results; SSE Riga in April.
Your diploma has to be recognised as part of every application. Start early.
The Art Academy of Latvia has no English-taught bachelor's degree.

language.englishTaughtBachelors: Available at the larger universities and the business schools; not at the Art Academy.

sectorLandscape.summary: Every Latvian higher education institution is an augstskola. The universitāte is the kind that offers academic as well as professional degrees; the other augstskolas, the akadēmijas and the koledžas offer professional programmes. The koledža is the one foreign guidance rarely mentions: a two-to-three-year first-level professional qualification that you can build on later.

routes.what: Academic and professional bachelor's degrees — the University of Latvia, Riga Technical University, Rīga Stradiņš and others. Where most English-taught bachelor's and Medicine sit.

Non-university institutions teaching professional bachelor's degrees, often more applied and more regional. Several private business schools, including SSE Riga and Turība, are in this group and teach in English.
routes.note: Also the umbrella word for all higher education institutions, which is confusing on first reading.

routes.what: Art and music academies admitting on portfolio or audition. The Art Academy of Latvia offers no English-taught bachelor's.
First-level professional higher education, two to three years after secondary school. Qualifies you to work in the occupation or to continue into a related higher education programme.
routes.note: Recorded so the route is visible. Not researched for international applicants.

notes: Not established: whether an EU citizen from Denmark can compete for Latvian state-funded (budget) places on an English-taught programme; whether institutions admit on predicted IB grades.
